descriptionChirho: A gentilic adjective and substantive designating a person of Aramean origin or the Aramean people collectively. Used with the article in the singular (ha-Arammi) to identify specific individuals: Bethuel and Laban as 'the Aramean' (Gen 25:20; 28:5; 31:20, 24), and Naaman 'the Aramean' (2 Kgs 5:20). Used without the article in Deuteronomy 26:5 ('a wandering Aramean was my father') to characterize ancestral Israelite identity. In the plural (Arammim) it refers to the Aramean people or military forces (2 Kgs 8:28-29; 9:15). The feminine form ha-Arammiyyah ('the Aramitess') in 1 Chronicles 7:14 designates a woman of Aramean descent. All these are inflectional and gender/number variants of one gentilic sense, not distinct lexical meanings.
